transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. I'm Ruth. Well, I work as a surveillance officer, and... what scared me enough to actually come in today is something happening at work. 

During the quiet stretches in the surveillance room, I keep hearing voices coming through the monitor speakers. They say things to me, like, "You missed it, Ruth," or "People are going to get hurt because of you." But the thing is, I know every channel is completely muted. And... no one else in the room hears anything at all. It's just me hearing it.
How long have you been hearing these voices—did they start recently, or have they been happening for weeks or months?
It's been going on for about four months now. It started right around the time I was promoted and moved into the lead casino surveillance role.
Have you been using any alcohol, recreational drugs, or new medications around the time these voices started, or at any point since?
No, nothing like that. I don't use any recreational drugs, and... I don't really drink alcohol either. As for medications, no, I haven't started taking anything new. Just my usual routine.
Over these past four months, have you also been feeling persistently sad, down, or losing interest and pleasure in things you used to enjoy?

Yes, actually. It's... well, most days I feel like this heavy, gray mood just settles over me before I even manage to get out of bed. It's hard to explain, but I just feel so down. And sometimes I'll just start tearing up in my car before my shift starts, over absolutely nothing... just seeing the casino lights can make me cry. I haven't really been enjoying much of anything lately.
Do you ever hear these voices during times when your mood feels okay or normal, or do they only happen when you're feeling really down?

No, they only happen when I'm feeling this low. Before this whole stretch of feeling so hopeless and... guilty, right after I took the surveillance lead job, I had never heard those accusations coming through the equipment. And I never felt so sure that I was a danger to everyone around me. The voices and all those beliefs, they really only seem to be tied to this same dark period.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a 4-month history of persistent depressed mood, anhedonia, tearfulness, and pervasive guilt, temporally coinciding with the onset of auditory hallucinations (accusatory voices) and delusional beliefs of being dangerous/responsible for harm. The psychotic symptoms are mood-congruent, occur exclusively during depressive episodes, and are absent when mood is euthymic, supporting Major Depressive Disorder with psychotic features rather than a primary psychotic or schizoaffective disorder. Substance use and medication causes were ruled out. No history of manic/hypomanic episodes or psychotic symptoms outside the mood episode was reported, arguing against schizoaffective disorder, and the persistence beyond one month argues against brief psychotic disorder.
